drifted.spec_text: A read timeout (`Completion::Timeout`) ... MUST NOT fail the drive's other jobs. Submission and draining continue, and after the loop each job whose segments did not all complete is reported `Err` with the timeout message — that job only (User Story 11 scenario 4).
drifted.actual: Completion::Timeout sets every still-Ok job of drive d to Err, fills obj_failed[d] and stops submissions to d; landed objects are not delivered; no incomplete-object pass (fix 8 reverted)

drifted.spec_text: the error is reported for that entry only; other entries in the batch continue to be processed independently
drifted.actual: true for a per-segment read error and a GPU copy error; a timeout, invalid tag, unexpected completion, disconnect or failed send fail every job of that drive

drifted.spec_text: Known gap, tracked as A-16: a call made while the drive list is being handed over can count the outgoing drives twice, so the next call can read lower.
drifted.actual: fold and swap/clear under one data_drives write guard; reader holds the read guard across baseline + live drives; gap closed

drifted_carried.note: worse: the only ServedBy::Ssd value test (repair_test_nvme_timeout_fails_whole_drive.rs) was deleted by 709153326; no Ssd, Remote, SizeMismatch tests

notes.text: An asynchronous lookup_async must hold the entry's read pin until its copy has completed (not merely queued) and record hit counters only then; lookup (src/lib.rs:2482-2493) inherits it. Today's synchronous code is safe (src/lib.rs:3429-3437). Deferred to the lookup_async issue.

lookup_async maps every dm.lookup error to KeyNotFound without retry (src/lib.rs:3500); documented in contracts/errors.md:37, so not drift; a writer-held live key reads as a miss on the single-key path. Decision needed, with the lookup_async issue.
